decisions.title: TVS2 replacement: Brightking SMAJ6.5A (C87267) replaces SD05 (C502527)
decisions.decision: Replace TVS2 SD05 (LCSC C502527) with Brightking SMAJ6.5A, LCSC C87267 (orderable model SMAJ6.5A/TR13), SMA (DO-214AC), fitted, on the +5V output rail.
decisions.rationale: Deterministic criteria walk over the three primary-sourced candidates (all retrieved 2026-08-14). (1) Standoff >= 6V: all pass; SMAJ6.5A has the largest margin -- VRWM 6.5V sits 1.5V over the 5.0V nominal and 1.3V over the L7805 guaranteed 5.2V band top, and its 7.22V breakdown minimum clears the band top by 2.02V. Since BB-2's defect is exactly conduction inside normal regulation (SD05: 0V margin nominal, -0.2V at band top), the standoff/breakdown gap is weighted first, and SMAJ6.5A doubles the 6.0V candidates' band-top clearance. (2) Clamp vs downstream abs-max chain: VC 11.2V at IPP 35.7A (10/1000us) crosses no retained downstream limit -- the L7805 bundle retains no output-pin abs-max (coverage gap, noted); the 0.9V VC penalty vs the 6.0V candidates (10.3V) is accepted. (3) Package/rework: SMA (DO-214AC) is the same D-FLAT footprint family already used by TVS1/TVS3/D5 -- no new footprint, larger hand-reworkable pads than SMF6.0A's SOD-123FL, and SMAJ-series naming consistency with TVS1/TVS3 (SMAJ15A). (4) Power class: 400W minimum on a fully specified 10/1000us waveform, matching the SMAJ15A family class; the FOSAN SMAJ6.0A's 400W has no stated pulse waveform in its datasheet, and SMF6.0A is 200W. (5) Leakage trade per BB-2: 500uA max at VRWM 6.5V vs the SD05's 10uA -- accepted as budgetable on the 500mA rail; the 5.0-5.2V operating point sits 1.3-1.5V below the knee, farther in relative terms than either 6.0V candidate, so the in-circuit leakage is plausibly the lowest of the three (not fact-provable, recorded as reasoning only). (6) Dated stock: 8,450 units at LCSC on 2026-08-14 -- second of the shortlist, ample for prototype quantities.

runners_up.reason: Best stock (148,360), lowest max leakage (400uA), lowest VC (10.3V), but SOD-123FL breaks the SMA/D-FLAT family shared by every other TVS position, 200W is half the board's protection class, and the standoff/band-top margin is the smallest that still passes.
Same SMA package and 400W class, but the FOSAN datasheet states no pulse waveform for its clamp/power rows, it has the highest max leakage (800uA), and the lowest stock (6,400).

decisions.title: Topology label verdict: LM2596S-ADJ inverting buck-boost (resolves #46's question)
decisions.decision: The canonical description of the -12V-rail converter is 'LM2596S-ADJ in inverting buck-boost configuration'. The schematic is authoritative: all three converter positions place zudo-pd:LM2596S-ADJ and no LM2586 symbol exists anywhere in the repo. Doc claims of 'LM2586SX-ADJ' are wrong on the chip, and 'inverted SEPIC' is wrong on the topology -- U4's manufacturer-documented arrangement (single inductor L3 to system GND, catch diode D3 to the negative output, device GND bootstrapped to -13.5V) is an inverting buck-boost, while a SEPIC requires two inductors (or a coupled pair) plus a coupling capacitor. Doc edits land in the wave-8 docs sub-issue (#126).
decisions.rationale: Schematic-vs-doc conflict resolves toward the schematic on three independent grounds: the placed symbols (property-level reads, three LM2596S-ADJ instances), the netlist-derived baseline reproducing the manufacturer-documented inverting buck-boost node arrangement (verified in the wave-5 review's locked-items table), and the absence of any LM2586 artifact in the repo. The wave-5 review re-verified U4's inverting referencing as LOCKED with catch-diode sense and inductor-to-GND arrangement exactly matching the LM2596 datasheet's inverting application section.

decisions.title: Q1 20V-contract gate guard: FITTED gate-source zener clamp provision (D8); NVM stays locked <= 15V
decisions.decision: Board A spec (#124) adds D8: a zener diode across Q1 gate-source (cathode to VBUS_IN / Q1 source, anode to Net-(Q1-G)), Vz window 10.4-11.6V (11V nominal, BZT52C11 class), SOD-123-class two-pad package, FITTED by default. Exact-orderable selection (manufacturer, LCSC number, primary datasheet, dated stock) is #124 scope under the same evidence discipline as the TVS2 pick -- no pre-researched candidate bundle exists for this slot, so locking an LCSC number here would be evidence-free. NVM stays locked <= 15V regardless. The complementary documented-note (program NVM before first attach to a >15V-capable source) goes to the docs pass (#126).
decisions.rationale: Why a fitted hardware guard rather than the DNP-provision or documented-note options: (1) BA-1's core finding is that a factory-default (unprogrammed) STUSB4500 advertises PDO3 = 20V/1A at highest priority, so the first plug-in of an assembled-but-unprogrammed Board A into a 20V-capable charger drives Vgs to -12.82V (0.82V past the +/-12V abs-max) with no hardware interlock -- a DNP part is absent in exactly that window, so DNP guards nothing, and the note-only option merely restates the procedural guard BA-1 already found insufficient. (2) The same divider reaches -20.77V during a D5 clamp event with VBEN asserted -- on a PROGRAMMED board at the legal 15V contract. No procedure can guard that path; only a fitted clamp bounds it. (3) Consistency: BA-1 is BLOCKER-class deterministic arithmetic of the same class as BB-1 (PTC1) and BB-2 (TVS2), both of which receive hardware fixes in this same decision set. Why this does not violate the locked '#90: do not touch the Q1 gate network': review finding BA-1 explicitly assigns the disposition to this wave-6 task ('reprogram-before-first-attach gate, divider change, clamp, or other mitigation' -- 'this is not a reopen'); the clamp is purely additive -- R11/R12 values and topology are untouched, the zener sits below its knee at the 15V operating point (|Vgs| 9.62V vs >= 10.4V minimum knee), and removing the two-pad part reverts to the exact v4-re-confirmed network. Clamp arithmetic: when conducting, zener current is limited by R12 (56k) to ~161uA at a 20V contract and ~382uA at the 32.4V clamp table point, holding |Vgs| ~10.4-11.2V -- inside the +/-12V abs-max in every reachable state. NEEDS BENCH residuals for the Board A bring-up plan: gate soft-start / turn-on behavior with the added junction capacitance; sub-knee zener leakage shifting the divider point (0.78V of margin between the 9.62V operating point and the 10.4V minimum knee is thin -- if bench shows conduction at 15V, step the window up one E24 value, e.g. 12V nominal, accepting clamp-at-abs-max-edge).

decisions.title: L7812 margin: math recorded; setpoint stays 13.5V -- explicitly NO spec change (NEEDS BENCH)
decisions.decision: NO spec change. R1 stays 10k; the U2 rail stays at the 13.53V setpoint in the Board B spec. The setpoint change candidate (e.g. R1 10k -> 11k, giving Vout = 1.23 x 12 = 14.76V and +2.76V of headroom at an added ~3.3W LDO dissipation at 1.2A) stays NEEDS BENCH per the locked #90 A5#1 deferral -- bench must first establish whether the L7812 actually drops out at real loads on a live rail.
decisions.rationale: The recorded math (BB-5): headroom 13.5 - 12.0 = 1.5V against the 2.0V TYPICAL dropout at 1A gives a -0.5V typical-value deficit, and DS0422 specifies no dropout figure at all at the 1.2A project load. Tolerance stacking makes it worse: the LM2596's +/-4% line/load tolerance puts the rail as low as 12.99V (deficit -1.01V), and the guaranteed VFB minimum (1.193V) alone gives 13.12V (deficit -0.88V). All of this is arithmetic on typical/limit values feeding an unverified upstream setpoint -- rule-ldo-dropout-chain refuses to promote it to a verdict, and no rail has ever been energized from a negotiated contract. The deficit is real on paper but the fix choice (raise the rail vs accept degraded PSRR-marginal operation vs an LDO part change) is a bench decision with a thermal cost attached; deciding it now would replace one unmeasured operating point with another.

decisions.title: PTC1 replacement: RUILON SMD1210P150TF/16 (C7529589) replaces SMD1210P200TF (C20808)
decisions.decision: Replace PTC1 SMD1210P200TF (LCSC C20808, Vmax 6VDC -- BLOCKER on the +12V rail) with RUILON SMD1210P150TF/16, LCSC C7529589 (Vmax 16V, Ihold 1.5A, Itrip 3.0A, 1210 package), fitted, on the +12V output rail. Board B spec (#125) scope.
decisions.rationale: Deterministic criteria walk, same discipline as the TVS2 pick. (1) Vmax >= rail: 16V gives +4V at the 12V nominal and +2.5V at the ~13.5V tripped-passthrough corner (U6 out of regulation) -- the same corner-margin class BB-8 records as passing for PTC3's identical 16V rating; the fitted part's -6V margin was the deterministic BLOCKER (rule-pptc-vmax-vs-rail refusal: replace before any rail power-on). (2) Hold fit: Ihold 1.5A >= the 1.2A rail budget with 0.3A (25%) margin at 25C -- passes the required gate. The hold-margin trade BB-1 flags (0.3A vs the P200TF's 0.8A) is weighed and accepted because no better 16V option exists in the package class: the RUILON table lists /16 suffixes only at the P150/P110 hold ratings (bundle SKILL.md), and a web check on 2026-08-14 confirms no SMD1210P200TF/16 orderable exists at LCSC -- the 2A/16V family member is SMD1812P200TF16 (C20812), an 1812 package requiring a footprint change, recorded as the fallback if bench shows nuisance trips. (3) Trip coordination: Itrip 3.0A (vs the P200TF's 4.0A) is more likely reachable by a fault fed through the L7812's internal current limit, improving the odds the PPTC actually trips rather than the LDO thermal-cycling indefinitely. (4) Package/footprint: 1210 unchanged (F1210 footprint coverage verified in the wave-4 library pass); same manufacturer, same primary-retained family datasheet as the fitted part. (5) Doc convergence: components/ptc-12v.md already documents this exact part (BB-10) -- the pick resolves that doc-vs-fitted mismatch in the doc's favor. Derating residual (NEEDS BENCH, BB-8 class): no 85C hold fact is retained for the /16 part; scaling the family's published derating (P200TF 2.0A -> 0.98A at 85C, 49%) estimates ~0.74A at 85C with the 1.2A crossing near ~48C ambient -- enclosure-ambient measurement belongs in the Board B bench plan, with the 1812 fallback as the escape hatch.

runners_up.reason: 2A hold at 16V but 1812 package -- breaks the 1210 constraint and requires a footprint change; recorded as the bench fallback if the P150TF/16 nuisance-trips at elevated ambient.

decisions.title: BB-3 disposition: U4 clamp-point overage accepted as transient-class residual; not bounded by decision (e)
decisions.decision: No part or topology change for U4. The -0.93V overage past U4's 45V absolute maximum (device-seen 45.93V = 32.4V clamp table point + 13.53V output magnitude) is accepted as a transient-class residual, recorded in the Board B spec notes and the bench plan (surge test must observe the U4 effective-input node). Decision (e) does NOT bound this exposure -- it clamps only the Q1 gate-source voltage, not VBUS; decision (d)'s C5/C7 swap restores positive input-capacitor margin (+2.6V) at the same table point. Revisit only if Board A layout later adopts a lower-clamping D5 (see ba2-disposition's recorded SMBJ20A upgrade path, which shrinks this overage at its source).
decisions.rationale: Both compared values are primary-sourced (45V abs-max; 32.4V table point), but the 32.4V figure is a 10/1000us waveform point at 12.3A, not the installed surge -- rule-u4-inverting-stress holds the comparison NEEDS BENCH. A 0.93V overage on a millisecond-class transient against an absolute-maximum (not operating) limit does not justify changing a LOCKED inverting topology whose referencing the review re-verified as correct; the #90 A2 text's '40V abs-max' defect (it is the operating maximum; abs-max is 45V, and the U4 comparison must add the output magnitude) is recorded for the docs pass via the review report.

decisions.title: BA-2 disposition: D5 stays SMAJ20A (locked #90); clamp-vs-28V overage accepted as mirror-conditioned residual; SMBJ20A recorded as the layout-phase upgrade path
decisions.decision: D5 stays SMAJ20A (LCSC C571370) -- the locked #90 A2 selection is unchanged and the BLOCKER-contradiction path is NOT triggered: BA-2 is a HIGH lead capped by mirror-only evidence, not a BLOCKER contradiction of a locked item. Options analysis recorded: (i) CHOSEN -- accept the 4.4V clamp-table-point overage against the STUSB4500 28V grouped abs-max as a transient-class residual, with the caveat that the 28V ceiling itself is UNSOURCED mirror evidence (primary DS12499 retrieval failed on both dated attempts) and 32.4V is a 10/1000us table point, not the installed waveform; (ii) SMBJ20A upgrade (floated in #90 itself): identical 20V standoff (BA-4 requires >= 20V to stay non-conducting at the 20V mis-contract edge, so no lower-standoff part is eligible), but the 600W class sits lower on its V-I curve at any given surge current, giving a lower real clamp -- deferred to Board A layout as the recorded upgrade path (SMB footprint change) where it can be adopted without reopening #90's electrical rationale; (iii) primary DS12499 retrieval to firm or move the 28V ceiling -- remains open. Bench scope: surge behavior observation on the dead v4 boards, which carry the identical network.
decisions.rationale: The #90 A2 residual text audits Q1's VDS overage but never mentions the STUSB4500 28V family -- BA-2's four-pins-across-two-states extension is new arithmetic, not a reopen. Severity stays HIGH (not BLOCKER) because the comparison ceiling is mirror-only and the stress is a rated-waveform table point; a part change on that evidence grade would swap a locked, bench-untested selection for an equally bench-untested one while the actual project gate (bench root-cause confirmation on v4 boards) is still open. Decision (e)'s fitted gate clamp independently removes the worst BA-2-adjacent consequence (the -20.77V gate-source transient); the remaining exposed pins (VDD, pin 18, DISCH) have no cheaper guard than a lower-clamping D5, which option (ii) provides at layout time.

decisions.title: -13.5V output-cap bank: add C12 (470uF/35V FOLLON C22387780) in parallel; C11 stays C2983319 on its Phi 8 land
decisions.decision: Add C12 = FOLLON EFVH035ADA471M10B0, LCSC C22387780, 470 uF / 35 V, Phi 10 x 10.5 case, fitted, in parallel on the '/DC-DC Conversion/-13.5V OUT' net (C12.2 on the rail, C12.1 on GND), at spec coordinate (38.1, 393.7). C11 is NOT swapped: it stays GVT1E477M0810CNVC / C2983319 on its Phi 8 CAP-SMD_BD8.0-L8.3-W8.3-LS9.0-FD land. The -13.5V output bank becomes C11 || C24 || C12 = 1410 uF total. No new symbol, footprint, inventory line, source, or candidate record is created -- C12 reuses the existing C22387780 line already fitted at C5/C7/C14/C20/C21/C24/C25.
decisions.rationale: Sizing target: every -13.5V output electrolytic at or below 85% of its 150 kHz-derated ripple rating at the rated load. LOAD DUTY: the worst-case 0.8 A is retained, not reduced -- -12V/0.8A is the published rail contract (board-b-synth-power.md product-rail line) and the whole downstream chain is already sized to it (PTC3 1.50 A hold, CJ7912 dropout evaluated at 0.8 A, the GND-return budget summing 1.2+0.8+0.5 A); nothing limits a user's module draw below the rated figure, so sizing to a smaller expected load would silently derate the published rail. The ripple figure is ideal-CCM (Iout*sqrt(D/(1-D))) and now credits the LM2596 switch-saturation voltage, which issue #171 identified as the dominant non-conservative omission and which is RESOLVED: fact-lm2596-vsat retains 1.16 V typical (fact-lm2596-vsat-max, 1.4 V at 25C / 1.5 V over temperature) from the hash-locked UMW datasheet's Electrical Characteristics 10.2 Saturation Voltage row, so D = (13.53 + 0.55) / (15 - 1.16 + 13.53 + 0.55) = 0.5043 and the output-cap ripple is 0.807 A, up from the 0.77 A the Vsat-free model gave. The remaining neglected inductor-ripple term is far smaller and runs the other way. ARITHMETIC: at 150 kHz ESR dominates each branch, so ripple divides as 1/ESR; retained max-ESR is 0.5079413077400916 Ohm (C2983319) vs 0.4515033846578592 Ohm (C22387780), an exact 1.125 ratio at identical 470 uF, giving an 8/26 : 9/26 : 9/26 split of 0.807 A -- C11 248.28 mA against its 312 mA rating (79.6%) and each of C24/C12 279.31 mA against 403 mA (69.3%). SENSITIVITY: at the guaranteed maximum Vsat the ripple reaches 0.817 A, putting C11 at 80.6% and C24/C12 at 70.2% -- every can still inside the 85% bar, which is what the bar was there to absorb. C11 is the binding member: at typical Vsat the +15 V input would have to sag to 13.29 V before C11 reaches 85% (C24/C12 not until 10.36 V); no retained fact bounds the +15 V rail low, so low line is not carried as a number here. The same model reproduces the as-built two-can numbers on their original Vsat-free basis (362.35 mA / 1.16x and 407.65 mA / 1.01x), which anchors it; those two figures are left on that basis as the historical as-built record. The 120 Hz-ESR caveat is carried: electrolytic ESR falls and flattens with frequency, so the absolute Ohm values are pessimistic while the RATIO between two same-technology, similar-size cans is the trustworthy part. VOLTAGE: the bank is deliberately mixed -- C11 at 25 V has 11.5 V margin on the 13.5 V-magnitude rail, C24/C12 at 35 V have 21.5 V; the weakest member passes at 1.85x the rail. RUNNERS-UP: (2) swapping C11 to a third C22387780 gives 63.7% per can but reverts C11's footprint Phi 8 -> Phi 10, undoing the just-landed issue #150 land correction whose own evidence names the Phi 8 land as the digit-for-digit match, and forces a rewrite of the Phi 8 comment in board_b_spec.py -- 12 points of margin nobody needs at that price; (3) swapping C11 without adding a can leaves 385 mA per can = 95.5%, which fails the 85% bar outright. A brand-new, not-yet-evidenced part was never reached because an evidenced-part bank clears the bar. ACCEPTED TRADE: output bulk rises 940 uF -> 1410 uF, which LENGTHENS the current-limited inverting-startup transient (~50% more charge to move at the same ~4.5 A limit, already 1.5 A over the 3.0 A PD contract) -- and PD sources fault on SUSTAINED overcurrent, so a longer window is the risk axis, not a higher peak. rule-inverting-startup-vs-pd-source already gates this domain NEEDS BENCH; the enlarged bank widens that existing bench item rather than opening a new one. STOCK: this raises the C22387780 count to 8 pieces/board against the 935-unit stock noted LOW by decision (d) at 7 pieces -- re-verify stock at order time. RESIDUAL: the installed ripple at C11/C24/C12 is still a bench measurement (BB-7); this decision resizes against the retained ratings, it does not measure.

decisions.title: Board P 20 V front end r2: reverse-blocking FET, UVLO at or above 4.5 V rising, single 100 uF bulk
decisions.decision: Coordinator phase-4 direction 2026-10-31 within the user-approved 20 V revision (dec-p-20v-revision). Q3 CSD18543Q3A C840100 is the SLVSE94G 8.3.5 blocking FET: source on connector-side VBUS_IN (U2 IN_SYS), drain on EF_IN (U2 IN 1/2), gate on EF_BGATE (U2 B_GATE). Q4 BSS138-7-F C40912 is the B_GATE pulldown: gate EF_DRV (U2 DRV), source VBUS_IN, drain EF_BGATE. UVLO R22/R23 becomes 11.5k C705719 / 4.02k C705781 0.1 % (rising 4.53-4.73 V, falling 4.20-4.45 V). Bulk on VBUS_P is the single C3 100 uF 50 V RVT1H101M0810 C970687; C4 is removed. All other dec-p-20v-revision values are unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Without Q3, U2 IN_SYS/IN are shorted and the protected node can back-feed the source; OSC proposes reverse current at most 1 mA. Q4 meets the datasheet pulldown rule (>= 15 V VDS, 20 V VGS, Ciss <= 50 pF, VGTH <= 3 V). The previous 10.5k/4.3k UVLO rose at 4.02-4.25 V, below the 4.5 V project floor; 11.5k/4.02k guarantees rising >= 4.5 V while falling 4.20-4.45 V remains a residual below 4.5 V. With 2 x 100 uF (up to 240 uF) the 5 V to 20 V PD transition at the source slew ceiling would draw about 7 A, above the 4.185 A I(OL) minimum; one 100 uF part (80-120 uF) limits it to about 3.6 A, while the hot-unplug overshoot estimate at 80 uF stays below the STUSB4500 28 V limit. The slew ceiling, ESR and overshoot terms are project assumptions; nothing is measured.

decisions.title: Board P 20 V / 5 A draft: proposed Q1 gate divider R11 150k / R12 4.7k with D8 BZT52C11-7-F clamp
decisions.decision: Coordinator phase-6 direction 2026-10-31 (draft, within dec-p-20v-revision): the Board P draft spec PROPOSES R11 (VBUS_P to Q1_G) 150k C22807, R12 (Q1_G to VBEN) 4.7k C23162 and a new D8 BZT52C11-7-F C92321 with cathode on VBUS_P and anode on Q1_G, the topology of Board A dec-e-q1-20v-gate-guard. C35 100 nF/50 V, Q1 DMP3036SFG-7 and the PCB are unchanged. The as-built Board P PCB keeps 100k/150k and no D8.
decisions.rationale: The 100k/150k divider gave -2.0 V at 5 V VBUS, inside the DMP3036SFG -1.0 to -2.5 V threshold range. The new open-clamp divider gives -4.606/-4.848/-5.090 V at 4.75/5.00/5.25 V; the guaranteed 29 mOhm RDS(on) row is at -5 V, which this divider reaches only above about 5.157 V VBUS and no divider can reach at 5.00 V nominal, but POWER_ONLY_ABOVE_5V keeps Q1 off at 5 V anyway. At 20 V the divider alone would give -19.39 V, so D8 conducts (about 1.97 mA at 20 V, 3.08 mA at the 25.208 V overshoot case) and holds |VGS| to 10.4-11.6 V, leaving at least 13.4 V to the 25 V VGSS. If D8 fails open the overshoot case gives -24.44 V, a 0.56 V margin. VBEN sinks up to 3.15 mA in total (D8 3.08 mA plus the R11 share); its rating is UNSOURCED. The turn-on gate time constant falls from 6.0 ms to 0.46 ms and the turn-off constant rises from 10 ms to 15 ms; the Board B input inrush at the faster turn-on against the TPS26630 I(OL) is not calculated. Nothing is measured.

decisions.title: Board P 20 V / 5 A draft: proposed Q1 Miller soft start (C36, Q5 body diode, R27) and 2 x 470R VBUS_VS_DISCH resistance
decisions.decision: Coordinator phase-7 direction 2026-10-31 after the independent review (finding 3 HIGH, finding 10 LOW), draft within dec-p-20v-revision: C36 CL10A105KB8NNNC C15849 1 uF from VBUS_OUT to Q1_MX, Q5 BSS138-7-F C40912 with gate and source on Q1_MX and drain on Q1_G (body diode Q1_MX to Q1_G), R27 0603WAF1503T5E C22807 150k from VBUS_P to Q1_MX, and R28 0603WAF4700T5E C23179 in series with R14 between U1.18 and VBUS_P. The as-built Board P PCB is unchanged.
decisions.rationale: With C35 gate-to-source only, the Q1 drain transition was Miller-limited by Q1's own Crss and lasted microseconds, so closing at 20 V dumped C3 into the uncharged Board B bank. C36 makes the drain slew equal the R12 gate current (3.45-4.0 mA at 20 V with a PA plateau of 1.5-3.5 V) divided by C36 (0.4-1.1 uF PA, the DC-bias curve is not in the bundle): 3.1-10 V/ms, at most 2.5 A into 250 uF, below the TPS26630 I(OL) 4.185 A minimum, so the eFuse does not current-limit and C3 does not charge-share. The Q5 diode blocks the reverse path, so a VBUS_P rise with Q1 off cannot pull Q1_G below the source; R27 recharges Q1_MX (tau 0.15 s) and assists turn-off. Q1 dissipates about 50 mJ per 20 V closure over 2.0-6.5 ms; DMP3036SFG SOA is not in the bundle (OPEN). R14 + R28 = 940 ohm keeps the VBUS_VS_DISCH current at 26.7 mA at 25.1 V, below the 50 mA maximum; the discharge time constant doubles against the 800 ms default (OPEN interaction). Nothing is measured.

decisions.title: 15 V Board P: r3 VDD feed and local clamp (R29 1k + R30 470R, D9 BZT52C18) on the top side
decisions.decision: Coordinator phase-17 direction 2026-11-01 (review F8, applied because it fits on the top side without moving any as-built part): U1.24 VDD moves from VBUS_IN onto VDD_LOC, fed through R29 0603WAF1001T5E C21190 1k and R30 0603WAF4700T5E C23179 470R in series (VDD_MID between them), with D9 BZT52C18-7-F C192739 (cathode VDD_LOC, anode GND). The as-built C2 100 nF stays at U1.24 and now decouples VDD_LOC; r3's C38 1 uF was not fitted in phase 17; phase 18 adds it (dec-p15-vdd-decoupling). VBUS_VS_DISCH, DISCH and VBUS_EN_SNK keep the as-built connections.
decisions.rationale: With VDD on VBUS_IN the 28 V VDD limit had +2.00 V at the SMAJ16A 26.0 V, 25 C point and -0.6 V at the TYP-based 28.6 V hot estimate (input-clamp-fix.md). calculate-input-ovp-20v.py stusb_local_clamp with the 1.47 kOhm feed gives a VDD pin bound of 20.802 V at 125 C with 28.6 V in (+7.198 V to 28 V; 20.721 V, +7.279 V at 26.0 V), from the guaranteed BZT52C18 VZ max and TC max rows; the D9 current at 28.6 V and -40 C is 8.82 mA. At a 4.72 V attach input VDD stays >= 4.373 V at the idle IDD maximum (0.273 V over the 4.1 V row) and 4.209 V at 2 x typical IDD; the active-communication IDD is not in the datasheet (OPEN). At 15 V the zener stays below its guaranteed VZ window at 25 C and above (VZ min 16.8 V). Phase 20 correction (review F7): a positive TC lowers VZ when cold, so the guaranteed minimum uses the TC maximum: VZ min 15.76 V at -40 C, only +0.01 V above a 15.75 V (+5 %) input (VDD_LOC itself sits 0.24-0.32 V lower at the idle IDD). Knee leakage at the cold +5 % corner is possible (IR 0.1 uA at 12.6 V and ZZK 225 Ohm at 1 mA are the only rows); sub-mA through 1.47 kOhm costs at most a few hundred mV of VDD, functionally benign. BZT52C20-7-F C260890 was evaluated (scripts/pcb/board-p15/zener-choice.py, boards/board-p15/d9-zener-choice.json): 23.041 V pin bound at 28.6 V / 125 C leaves 4.959 V to 28 V (< 5 V required) and its 22.64 V VZ max at 105 C exceeds the 22 V VDD operating row, so BZT52C18 stays. The phase-17 omission of C38 is superseded by dec-p15-vdd-decoupling. Nothing is measured.

decisions.title: 15 V Board P: r3 C38 1 uF VDD_LOC decoupler on the top side

The feed and C2 + C38 (1.1 uF nominal) form a tau of about 1.62 ms (phase 20 correction of the earlier 1.47 ms, review F8); DS12499 Rev 7 gives no VDD ramp or UVLO requirement to check it against (UNKNOWN); the attach-time VDD rise and its effect on the STUSB4500 start-up are not in the evidence (OPEN). VBUS_VS_DISCH: R14 + R28 become 2 x 1k C21190 and D10 BZT52C20-7-F C260890 clamps U1.18. DISCH: R13 becomes 0603WAF4701T5E C23162 4.7k and D12 BZT52C18-7-F clamps U1.9. VBUS_EN_SNK: Q6 BSS138-7-F C40912 cascode (source VBEN_PIN = U1.16 with D11 BZT52C18-7-F and J3.8, drain VBEN = R12, gate VG_LOC = VDD_LOC through R31/R32 0603WAF1003T5E C25803 100k/100k). decisions.rationale: The 28 V STUSB pin limit was the binding constraint on the main surge path (rule-tvs-clamp-vs-absmax). With mA-level series feeds into guaranteed zener rows (DS18004 VZ max at IZT plus TC max), the pin bound is 20.709 V (VDD) and 23.0 V (VBUS_VS_DISCH) with VBUS_P at the 28.35 V TVS2200 35 A / 125 C row, and VDD stays <= 20.38 V at 105 C, inside the 22 V operating row. decisions.title: B20 RDY timing resistors: RRDY1/RRDY2 2 x 150k C22807 replace 2 x 100k C25803 (readiness D11)
decisions.decision: Owner decision 2026-11-12 JST by the campaign manager (coordinator) under Takazudo's delegation of the owner design decisions, relayed 2026-11-11 20:38Z. It supersedes the 200 kOhm RDY network (two 0603WAF1003T5E C25803 100k in series into CRDY C13585 10 uF) used since phase 9. Raise the RDY timing resistance and keep CRDY, the 0.5 V / 1.5 V Q37 thresholds and the 5x servo-settle PROJECT screen unchanged. Selection rule: the smallest standard value, preferring the project inventory with the same package and tolerance, for which the earliest-RDY short corner exceeds the 5x settle screen by at least 5 %. The short corner applies high P5_SUP, the 0.5 V PA threshold, R -1 %, C -10 %, X5R TCC -15 % and TYPICAL DC bias. Two inventory 0603 1 % parts give 250k (1.019x, fails) or 300k; 300k (2 x 0603WAF1503T5E C22807, already fitted as RHO1/RHO2) gives 0.23466 s against 0.1919 s (1.2228x). The smallest non-inventory alternative, 100k + 158k E96 (1.052x), would add a new orderable line. Value-only change on the existing R0603 footprints.
decisions.rationale: The 2026-11-11 tolerance-corner run failed the 5x settle screen at 0.18405 s, and adding the sourced -15 % TCC term puts it at 0.15644 s. At 300k the long corner (low P5_SUP, 1.5 V maximum threshold, R +1 %, C +10 %, TCC +15 %) is 1.39191 s. No upper bound is violated. The canonical interface (OSC 433c88b pd-interface-20v.md, SHA-256 8702890d...56a) sets no maximum detect-to-enable delay and no slowest-ramp bound (section 5: 'No upper bound in the contract'). POR ends by 0.0464 s and the min-off hold by 0.12104 s, both before the earliest RDY. RDY reset goes through Q36 directly, not through RRDY. No phase33 deck or generator models the RDY RC. Q36 drain and Q37 gate leakage at the RDY node are not in the bundle (UNSOURCED); a higher R makes the node more leakage-sensitive. The 5x factor remains a PROJECT screen, the DC-bias data is typical, and nothing is measured.

decisions.title: B20 OV/UV comparators: 100k 0402 C25741 in series with the four U6/U7 divider-side inputs; U8 unchanged (readiness D12)
decisions.decision: Owner decision 2026-11-12 by the campaign manager (coordinator) under Takazudo's delegation of the owner design decisions. Fit one 0402WGF1003TCE C25741 100k (R0402) between each U6/U7 window-divider node and its comparator input: RS12O OV12_DIV to OV12_IN (U6.3), RS12U UV12_DIV to UV12_IN (U6.6), RS5O OV5_DIV to OV5_IN (U7.3), RS5U UV5_DIV to UV5_IN (U7.6); annotated R77-R80. U8 (-12) is left unresistored. The absent / discharge levels are taken to apply to a disabled, unloaded terminal (the conservative reading). A true comparator is not pursued. Package amendment 2026-11-12 (same delegation): the 0603 C25803 first chosen was changed to 0402 C25741 because a placement search found only two 0603 sites near U6/U7 that clear existing courtyards and other-net copper, while 0402 sites exist 2-3.5 mm from all four pins; the resistors dissipate microwatts with well under 1 V across them, and short *_IN stubs keep the 3 pF stray assumption. Value, 1 % tolerance and 100 ppm/C TCR are unchanged, so the CALCULATED results stand.
decisions.rationale: SBOS807E 7.3.7 gives back-to-back differential input diodes, recommends limiting input current to 10 mA and names an input series resistor as the remedy; the diode forward voltage is not stated (0.4-0.7 V PA). CALCULATED with no external load after the discharge hold-up: before the fix the diodes back-feed +12 to 0.915-1.162 V and +5 to 1.467-1.78 V; with the four resistors +12 is 0.124-0.253 V and +5 0.158-0.307 V, below the 0.5 / 0.6 V levels. With 100k also on U8 the -12 terminal rose to 0.302-0.601 V, bounded only by the unsourced Q55 body-diode drop, which reached the 0.6 V stop limit, so U8 keeps its diodes clamping the REF-referenced -12 dividers (0.204-0.357 V). No resistor path from U8's inputs reaches the +12 / +5 terminals, P5_SUP or M12_PRE without passing through REF25 or GND (FET, diode and op-amp paths not walked). IB x (Thevenin + R_S) on the -40..125 C rows (5 nA U6/U7, 7.5 nA U8) leaves every OV/UV window inside its limits; those rows are specified at VCM = VS / 2, and U8's inputs sit near GND, about 4.6 V from its supply midpoint, so its IB row is applied outside the stated condition; the tightest margin is OV -12 high at 0.197 % with the full-range REF5025 budget. The added input RC is at most 1.8 us on SBOS807E typical input capacitance plus a 3 pF stray PA; the project has no OV response budget. REF25 diode loading falls from 0.93 to 0.17 mA.
